check_prompts.md: the body-view signal has_prompt_blocks=false, confirmed by direct grep (no '**Prompt**' label, no '{{prompt:' marker anywhere in the raw source). All 6 fences in this file are literal CLI/slash commands the student types directly into a terminal or the Claude Code CLI (`gh auth status`, `claude mcp add ...`, `/mcp`, `/plugin marketplace add ...`) -- this is a flat quick-reference lookup (curriculum/CLAUDE.md: 'Quick reference -- flat lookup. No progression'), not an exercise/lecture with student-pasted-to-Claude prompt blocks. All 49 check_prompts.md rules are therefore N/A on that single structural ground; individual rows below note it without re-litigating per rule.

Non-blocking observation (not filed as a finding -- no harm found): Claude Code's VS Code extension shipped an 'Add server form' in its MCP servers dialog (v2.1.248/v2.1.260, confirmed via live changelog fetch this session) -- a GUI form for adding an arbitrary MCP server outside a plugin. The file's 'What Claude Code doesn't do yet' section (line 118) says 'no in-CLI picker ... outside of a plugin' and describes Desktop's connector panel -- both claims stay literally true (AE101 is CLI+Desktop only per curriculum/CLAUDE.md, no VS Code in scope), so this doesn't misdescribe the training's own platform. Flagging for awareness only in case VS Code enters scope later.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify capabilities BEFORE asserting, not after.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 54 fence `claude mcp add --transport http jira https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2` and line 62 'The current canonical endpoint is `/v1/mcp/authv2`' (echoed in the maintainer stamp, line 141, checked 2026-07-26) assert v1/mcp/authv2 as canonical. Live re-verification this session (two independently-neutral WebFetches against https://support.atlassian.com/rovo/docs/getting-started-with-the-atlassian-remote-mcp-server/, worded to avoid priming per check_research_claims §15) both returned the SAME result: Atlassian's current docs give `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp` as the endpoint, with the exact Claude Code install line `claude mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`, and state v1 will auto-upgrade to v2 tools starting 2027-03-01 (i.e. v1 is now the legacy path, not the canonical one the docs lead with). This is exactly the trigger the file's own maintainer block names for an update ('Atlassian ... ship an MCP change (new endpoint, deprecated endpoint ...)'). Harm: a student pasting line 54 verbatim lands on a soon-to-be-superseded endpoint that the vendor's own current docs no longer present as canonical -- the rule's audit-mode clause ('embedded platform claims ... = assertions still needing verification, not established context') applies squarely here. Cross-checked GitHub (api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/, trailing slash) and Linear (mcp.linear.app/mcp, readonly variant, /sse deprecated) the same way -- both still match the file exactly, so this is a single-vendor drift, not a pattern.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Update the CLI install line and the 'current canonical endpoint' sentence to `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp` (Atlassian's own install example even renames the connector `atlassian` rather than `jira`); refresh the source-verification stamp's date/result for that entry and add a note about the 2027-03-01 v1-to-v2 auto-transition so the file's own history of endpoint churn (v1/sse -> v1/mcp/authv2 -> v2/mcp) stays legible.
